content:
Valid values are found by checking prime candidates \(p,q\).

- \(a=4\): \(p=3,q=5\) give \(3,5,13,29\), all prime.
- \(a=6\): \(p=5,q=11\) give \(5,11,31,127\), all prime.
- \(a=10\): \(p=3,q=7\) give \(3,7,19,59\), all prime.

For other \(a\in[1,10]\), there is at most one prime \(p\) with \(p^2+a\) prime, so two distinct \(p,q\) cannot be found.

Thus the required sum is \(4+6+10=20\).

\[
\boxed{20}
\]
